([[Milford, Connecticut]]) | draft_year = 2005 | career_start = 2005 | career_end = 2011 | career_number = 35 | career_position = [[Power forward (basketball)|Power forward]] | years1 = {{nbay|2005|start}} | team1 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years2 = 2006 | team2 = [[Dodge City Legend]] | years3 = 2006–2007 | team3 = [[Wilmington Sea Dawgs]] | years4 = 2007 | team4 = [[Albany Patroons]] | years5 = 2007–2008 | team5 = [[Śląsk Wrocław (basketball)|Śląsk Wrocław]] | years6 = 2011 | team6 = [[BC Naglis|Palangos Naglis]] | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season blocks leaders|NCAA blocks leader]] (2005) * 3× MAAC Defensive Player of the Year (2003–2005) }} '''Deng Nathaniel Magany Gai''' (born March 22, 1982) is a South Sudanese former professional [[basketball]] player. A [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]], he briefly played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and in several other leagues. Gai was the 2005 [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season blocks leaders|NCAA blocks leader]]. ==Early life== Gai fled from Sudan in 1999 as a refugee due to the [[Second Sudanese Civil War|civil war]].{{cite web |last1=Tommelleo |first1=Donna |title=From Sudan to Fairfield, Gai chasing NBA dream |url=https://sudantribune.com/spip.php?iframe&page=imprimable&id_article=7810 |website=Sudan Tribune |access-date=November 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110216191946/https://sudantribune.com/spip.php?iframe&page=imprimable&id_article=7810 |archive-date=February 16, 2011}} He travelled by train and a crude boat over a three-day trek to Egypt. Gai arrived in the United States and settled in [[Fairfield, Connecticut]]. ==College basketball== After attending [[Milford Academy]] in [[Connecticut]], Gai played [[college basketball]] at [[Fairfield University]] (also in the state), where he was a three-time MAAC Defensive Player of the Year and took the [[Fairfield Stags men's basketball|Stags]] to the [[Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference|MAAC]] semifinals in 2005.[http://vault.sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1108795/index.htm Andrea Woo, "Hard Road to Hardwood Glory,"] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120729101451/http://vault.sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1108795/index.htm |date=2012-07-29 }} [[Sports Illustrated]], March 14, 2005 Gai graduated as number eight on the [[NCAA]]'s all-time [[block (basketball)|blocked shots]] list. As a senior, Gai was named first team All-MAAC, leading the nation in blocks (5.5 bpg) while blocking 10 or more shots in three contests.{{Cite web |url=http://fairfieldstags.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/gai_deng00.html |title=CSTV.com: #1 in College Sports |access-date=2007-07-05 |archive-date=2007-02-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070210204313/http://fairfieldstags.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/gai_deng00.html |url-status=dead }} ==Professional basketball== Gai declared for the [[NBA draft]] [[2004 NBA Draft|in 2004]], but ultimately withdrew his name.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2004/early_040618.html |title=Fifty-three early entry candidates withdraw |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2008-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020181612/http://www.nba.com/draft2004/early_040618.html |archive-date=2012-10-20 |url-status=dead }} He was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2005.[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/free_agents_050805.html Sixers sign free agents Deng Gai and Shavlik Randolph] After playing in only two regular-season games for the team, Gai was waived in December 2005. He then briefly played for the [[United States Basketball League|USBL]]'s [[Dodge City Legend]] and the [[American Basketball Association (2000-)|ABA]]'s [[Wilmington Sea Dawgs]]. Subsequently, Gai, who had been drafted in 2005 by the [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]]'s [[Albany Patroons]] (2nd round, 10th overall), played for the team in the USBL, leading it in blocks. At the end of the season, he was named to the league's All-Defensive Team.[http://www.usbl.com/currentNews.php?news_id=235 USBL reveals 2007 “ALL-USBL” teams] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606180026/http://www.usbl.com/currentNews.php?news_id=235 |date=2011-06-06 }} In 2007–08, Gai represented [[Poland]]'s [[Śląsk Wrocław (basketball)|Śląsk Wrocław]], but the team folded after that season. ==Personal life== Gai has nine siblings.
